title: Account Priority Token Economy and Runway Scheduling
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success continue to request ad-hoc VIP commitments for large accounts. Engineering and Product capacity are strained by last-minute scope additions with unclear priority, leading to missed delivery expectations and unpredictable roadmap churn.

Goal: Design and pilot an ‘Account Priority Token Economy’ that quantifies and schedules high-touch commitments for top accounts into a predictable runway. The system should translate customer urgency and contract weight into redeemable tokens, map tokens to sprint credit windows, and surface an operational schedule for Product, Eng, and Solutions to plan around.

Objectives:
- Reduce unplanned roadmap churn from VIP requests by 60% in pilot cohort.
- Provide visibility into commitment runway for Sales and CS with an SLA-backed response time (initial triage within 48 hours).
- Formalize tradeoffs (scope, quality, time) through token-to-sprint-credit conversions tied to effort estimates.
- Instrument metrics for revenue retention influenced by commitment delivery.

Scope (what we will do in the pilot):
- Define token issuance rules: contract size, escalation level, executive sponsorship, urgency.
- Token catalogue mapping to sprint credits (e.g., 1 token = 2 dev-days of scoped delivery) and permissible feature classes.
- Runway scheduler: a lightweight calendar view in Console that reserves sprint capacity per cycle and shows token redemptions and remaining headroom.
- Intake form updates (Support portal + Solutions intake) to capture token requests and mandatory acceptance criteria (OKR alignment, success metrics).
- Commitment SLA playbook for PM/Eng/CS collaboration (triage workflow, go/no-go gating, fallback policies).

Out of scope for pilot: automated billing changes, on-prem deployment of the scheduler, deep legal contract edits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pilot implemented for 5 strategic accounts across Sales and Customer Success.
- Console runway view shows token reservations per upcoming 2 cycles and is updated via intake form.
- Triage SLA (48h) met on average for token requests in pilot window.
- Engineering retrospective after pilot demonstrates >=60% reduction in last-minute scope insertions.
- Stakeholder signoff from Sales lead, CS director, Eng manager, and Security (if applicable).

Success metrics:
- Number of emergency (same-cycle) VIP commits reduced by 60%.
- % of token redemptions that meet agreed acceptance criteria >= 80%.
- Renewal expansion delta attributable to committed deliveries (tracked via sales ops) >= 2% for cohort.

Proposed solution (implementation sketch):
1) Token Model: score incoming requests by account tier, contract ARR, executive backing, and business impact. Translate score to token allotment.
2) Sprint Credit Conversion: map tokens to discrete sprint-credit buckets with caps per cycle to prevent overcommitment.
3) Runway Scheduler UI: new Console mini-view that overlays token reservations on cycle calendars and flags capacity conflicts.
4) Intake + Triage Flow: intake form with mandatory success criteria + auto-assign to on-call PM for triage. Triage outputs a ticket with a token redemption line item.
5) Reporting and Audit: token ledger exported weekly for finance and CS reconciliation.

Dependencies: ["ENG-1842", "ENG-2709", "PM-210314", "PM-421987"]

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Tokens perceived as transactional bribes, not strategic agreements. Mitigation: Require OKR alignment and executive sponsor signoff for issuance.
- Risk: Over-issuance leads to capacity collapse. Mitigation: Hard caps per cycle, visible runway warnings in Console.
- Risk: Legal/contract conflicts. Mitigation: Queue legal review for tokens that imply changes in contractual SLAs.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-2: Finalize token rules, sprint-credit mapping, intake form prototype.
- Week 3-5: Build minimal Console runway view (read-only) and triage workflow.
- Week 6-10: Pilot with 5 accounts; weekly sync with Sales/CS.
- Week 11: Evaluate pilot, collect metrics, decision gate for wider rollout.

Stakeholders: ["Sarah Lin (Sales Ops)", "Diego Morales (Head of CS)", "Nina Park (Engineering Manager)", "Raymond Cho (Legal advisor)", "Marco Ruiz (PM lead)"]

Open questions:
- What is the canonical authority to revoke tokens if delivery risks spike?
- Should tokens expire? Proposed: tokens expire after 4 cycles unless otherwise negotiated.
- Billing/finance process for reserved runway (charge or no charge during pilot)?
